name: Mata Ortiz, on the road south
synopsis: At midday Billy watches the opera caravans leave the hacienda on this road south. Two days later the brothers follow it, loaded with food the ejido workers have pressed on them and with “the girl” riding behind Boyd. They stop at noon by the river to eat and sleep under the trees.

name: The opera company stranded on the Madera road
synopsis: The horses balk where the troupe has halted in a field of flowers, its men two days gone to Madera after a drunken muleteer hacked a mule to death on the road. From her hammock the primadonna talks of masks and jealousy, and warns the brothers that so long a search is hard even for brothers to share.

name: Camps by the river
synopsis: “The girl” cooks for them in an oak grove by the river. Next day, at a ford where naked boys swim below a culvert, Billy drives a nail down inside Boyd's boot with the shotgun barrel and admits he saw the primadonna bathing.

name: Crossing of the old wagon road to Namiquipa
synopsis: Watering the horses in the river, Billy talks crops, oxen and home with an old man who promises to pray for him. That night Boyd says “the girl” wants to go to her mother in Namiquipa. In the morning they give her a horse and half their money, and she rides off east alone.

name: Las Varas
synopsis: After two hungry days in the cold pinewoods they ride in past the maize warehouses and the station. In an unheated café the chicken enchiladas prove inedible, so they scrape them into their pot for a three-legged dog, while two locals are served rich plates of goat.

name: The steer herd on the road to La Boquilla
synopsis: Towards evening vaqueros pass with about a thousand wild steers, three days out from La Quemada and bound for the stock pens at Naco on the border. The brothers watch from high ground as the herd drifts west, then ride on after dark through a hamlet of log houses.

name: The road north of the Babícora lake
synopsis: Next morning Niño, Bailey and Tom come up wet from the lake with other horses, driven by two young vaqueros. With Billy holding the shotgun, Boyd ropes Niño and Bailey and Billy cuts out Tom. One vaquero rides off for help while the other trails them along the road.

name: In sight of the Boquilla hacienda
synopsis: Five riders block the road ahead and three close in behind. Their one-armed leader takes Niño's papers, calls them worthless and, because the boys are young, brings no charges but sends them to a señor López at Babícora. At Billy's word the brothers turn Niño and Bailey loose.

name: Following the horses' tracks north
synopsis: Back where they first met the horses, Boyd finds the tracks leaving the road north. At twilight they glimpse the riders with a dozen horses miles ahead, and they stop in a swale on a pitch-black night, Billy sleeping with the horse's rope tied to the saddle under his head.

name: Quijada's remuda
synopsis: The tracks lead to a road and a crossroads where Quijada, Mr Simmons' superintendent of the Nahuerichic, sits waiting. He leads them up the road to the remuda and lets Boyd rope Niño, Bailey and Tom out of the herd, then writes Billy a note for the horses, which Billy tucks in his hatband.

name: La Boquilla
synopsis: The brothers ride in at noon driving their horses, and Billy buys forty feet of grass rope for hackamores. The woman at the store tells him the cloth a young girl has just bought, with her wedding savings, is to line her father's coffin.

name: Off the road north of La Boquilla, west to a river
synopsis: A mile out of town they turn west to the river with nine horses, Boyd having driven off the riders' mounts in the confusion in the street. At dusk Billy takes the one-armed man's pistol, saying he will return it, and herds the five Boquilla horses over a rise and back towards the town.

name: The dry camp after the night ride
synopsis: Towards dawn they stop in an old burn on a rise with no water or grass. Billy tells Boyd he found Niño's papers in the one-armed man's saddlebag and kept the pistol after all. At daylight he proposes riding north to hide at the hacienda, and when Boyd says they are to meet “the girl” the next day, Billy says it can't be helped.

name: San José
synopsis: Finding no road across the river, they follow it north to a hamlet of grey mud huts where women watch warily from doorways. A woman feeds them cold atole in clay bowls and refuses payment, and when Billy offers it for her children she says she has none.

name: The river camp near San José
synopsis: They camp and swim among the cottonwoods. At dawn Billy leaves Boyd the pistol and goes after ducks, then sees five riders on the far bank and races back, but a rifle shot from across the river hits Boyd as he brings in the horses. Billy shouts their surrender, the firing goes on, and he flees with Boyd on Niño.

name: The dirt road in open country
synopsis: Chased across the plain, Billy passes Bailey, lamed by a bullet, and makes for a road he sees a vehicle crossing. Farmworkers on a brakeless flatbed lift Boyd aboard and head north, two riders cutting away after them. Billy outruns the rest but loses Bird, and never sees Tom again.

name: The blind man's house
synopsis: Near midnight a woman takes Billy in and gives him milk and eggs. She tells how her husband lost his eyes to a German officer after a failed rebel attack on Durango in 1913 and walked blind towards Parral, and the blind man adds his own thoughts on darkness, the world and justice.

name: The desert crossroads on the main road north
synopsis: Riding on, Billy is rejoined by Boyd's dog, cut up from a fight, and before noon he meets the main road to Casas Grandes at an empty crossroads. He sleeps in a field, dreams of wolves and of Boyd begging him not to leave, and rides all next day through rain.

name: Mata Ortiz, the blue tienda
synopsis: Billy asks at a blue tienda for a doctor and learns the nearest is in Casas Grandes. The old woman there tells him his brother was alive when the truck went by, and a shy girl gives him a small silver heart, a milagro for the wounded boy.

name: San Diego, after dark
synopsis: The Muñoz woman is waiting at her door, and Boyd lies inside on a pallet ringed with the workers' gifts under a single candle. No doctor has seen him, only an old healer with herb poultices and tea. Boyd says it is his fifteenth birthday, and the woman cannot answer when Billy asks how bad it is.

name: Casas Grandes at 3 a.m.
synopsis: Billy crosses the railway embankment into the sleeping town and follows Alameda Street to a lit cantina. He wakes the only man in it, asleep at a table, and asks where the doctor lives.

name: Back to San Diego, in the doctor's car
synopsis: The doctor will not take Niño as payment and drives Billy back to the ejido in his old Dodge. With Billy holding Boyd's hand he cleans both wounds, cuts away dead flesh and dresses them, and finds the boy lucky: the lungs and great artery are untouched and there is little infection. He leaves at first light, promising to return.

name: San Diego, leaving at dusk
synopsis: Billy sets out at dusk, refusing the Muñoz woman's plea to wait for morning, with food she has packed for him. He checks that the pistol lies under Boyd's pillow and learns that men have come to the ejido twice. She shrugs off the danger and counts Boyd as one of their own.

name: Mata Ortiz
synopsis: He rides through the town in the dark and keeps on until the moon is high, then leaves the road to sleep until daylight in a grove he had spotted against the sky.

name: Within earshot of the Las Varas crossing
synopsis: Towards evening the workers' truck that carried Boyd to San Diego pulls up beside him and the men on its bed shake his hand. They have seen Boyd that day and tell a heroic story of him shooting the manco at Boquilla, which Billy tries to play down. In the night a passing train shakes the ground and wakes him, then whistles for the Las Varas crossing.

name: La Boquilla at noon
synopsis: He rides into town at midday, shotgun laid over the saddle, finds no one about, and turns south. Towards dark he meets young men riding north to a Saturday dance and watches each of them closely as they pass.

name: La Pinta by moonlight
synopsis: The moon is up when he rides through La Pinta, on its upland of juniper above the Santa María valley.

name: Santa Ana de Babícora at midnight
synopsis: He reaches the town at midnight and finds it dark and deserted. He waters the horse in the little alameda and takes the road west for Namiquipa.

name: A stream of the Santa María headwaters
synopsis: He sleeps by the stream an hour west of town and wakes late. After he washes in the creek, “the girl” rides by in a new blue dress, on the horse that was his mother's. He catches her up, and when he swears Boyd is alive she kneels in the road to pray.

name: Back through Santa Ana
synopsis: They ride back through the town near noon, “the girl” keeping her distance behind him. North of it they eat her food in an acacia grove, where she speaks of her thrice-widowed grandmother's views on men and says the whole country believes Boyd killed the manco. Later she stops to scold three girls walking to Soto Máynez.

name: La Boquilla after dark
synopsis: They come through the town after dark, Billy holding the shotgun upright as before. Where the manco fell, “the girl” crosses herself and kisses her fingers. A trash fire on the edge of town makes them wary, but no one is near it.

name: Camp at the edge of the lake
synopsis: They camp in a hollow by the lake and finish her food, and she tells him God's care reaches everyone. Billy wakes in the night from a dream of holding his dying brother in a dark city, and kneels by the water until dawn as scenes from his travels pass before him.

name: Las Varas
synopsis: Hungry, they buy beans, tortillas and tamales in the quiet town. The opera company's arriero finds them and says the troupe waited by the road for a man who went off with the money, and is now stranded. “The girl” gives him coins, which annoys Billy, and he rides north without waiting to see if she follows.

name: Camp on the river south of Mata Ortiz
synopsis: On the last night of the three-day ride north he refuses her wish to push on to the ejido in the dark. They camp on a gravel bar, eat the last of the beans by a driftwood fire, and watch cranes pass high overhead going south.

name: San Diego, on a feast day
synopsis: They ride in at noon on a feast day, with workers idle in their doorways. Billy goes into the Muñoz house first and finds Boyd sitting up against the wall, but Boyd's first words are for “the girl”, asking where she has been.

name: Cuauhtémoc, as far south as he rides
synopsis: Billy wakes one morning to find Boyd and “the girl” gone, and rides south alone with the shotgun ready. Weeks of searching turn up only rumours, and Cuauhtémoc is the farthest south he goes.

name: Namiquipa
synopsis: He turns north again to Namiquipa, “the girl”'s home, but no one there will admit to knowing her.

name: La Norteña, as far west as he rides
synopsis: His search reaches west as far as La Norteña and the divide. By now he is gaunt and grey with dust, and there is still no sign of them.

name: The crossroads at Buenaventura
synopsis: One red dawn he waits on horseback where the roads cross at Buenaventura, watching flights of wildfowl pass over the river and its lagoons.

name: Álamo
synopsis: Heading back north he passes again through this small mud hamlet on the mesa. People remark on his return, and his wandering starts to turn into a story told about him.

name: Galeana
synopsis: He passes back through Galeana, another place he has seen before, where his return is noticed too. It is early December, and the nights on the high plains are cold, with almost nothing to keep out the chill.

name: Casas Grandes, December
synopsis: Two days without food, he reaches the town after midnight in a cold rain and knocks at the doctor's gate. He tells the mozo that Boyd recovered and then vanished, and asks to see the doctor, but the doctor is dead. Billy offers his sympathy and rides back down the dark street.

name: The dirt road in open country
synopsis: Shot through the body, Boyd is lifted from Niño's saddle onto a farmworkers' flatbed and laid on their shirts and serapes. Billy cannot tell whether he is alive or dead as the truck grinds on north, two of the riders cutting away to follow it.

name: Mata Ortiz, the truck passing
synopsis: The truck carries Boyd north through the town. The old woman at the blue tienda later tells Billy that he was alive as it passed her door, and that people walked after it to the edge of town.

name: San Diego, the Muñoz house
synopsis: The workers bring Boyd to the ejido, where he is laid on a pallet in the Muñoz house. With no doctor to be had, an old woman binds his wounds with herb poultices and gives him tea, and the truck comes back with workers who leave gifts of food, flowers and holy images around him.

name: Namiquipa, the mother of “the girl”
synopsis: Boyd and “the girl” slip away from San Diego while Billy sleeps, and he cannot learn where they have gone. Namiquipa is the likeliest place, since “the girl” wanted to visit her mother there. When Billy searches the town, no one will admit to knowing her.
